results.question: How much is the monthly fee on the everyday account and how do I avoid paying it?
results.answer:
The Kaskazi Everyday Account costs KES 250 a month. You don't pay it in any month when either of two waivers applies:

- **Salary:** The KES 250 monthly fee is waived for any month in which your salary is paid into your Kaskazi Everyday Account. Pay from a friend, a mobile money wallet, or your own transfers from another account doesn't count.
- **Average balance:** The KES 250 monthly fee is also waived for any month in which your average balance is KES 50,000 or more. Kaskazi Bank adds up the balance in your Kaskazi Everyday Account at the end of each day of the month, then divides by the number of days in the month.

You only need one of these. I can check your current balance or recent transactions if you'd like to see how close you are.

results.question: what happens to my student account when I turn 26
results.answer:
When you turn 26, your Kaskazi Student Account becomes a Kaskazi Everyday Account automatically the month after your 26th birthday, or earlier if you can no longer show a valid student ID, whichever comes first. Kaskazi Bank tells you in the app before the change happens.

Your account number, debit card and PIN, balance, standing orders and app login all stay the same. The Kaskazi Everyday Account monthly fee of KES 250 applies, unless your salary is paid into the account that month or your average balance for the month is KES 50,000 or more. The card's standard daily ATM limit of KES 100,000 applies instead.

To avoid the fee, you can ask your employer to pay your salary into your former Student Account, which is now a Kaskazi Everyday Account.

results.question: what happens if i miss one instalment on my personal loan
results.answer:
If an instalment isn't paid in full on its date, it counts as missed. A late payment fee of KES 500 is charged for each missed instalment, and interest continues on what you owe. The fee is charged once for that instalment, however long the instalment stays unpaid.

We try to collect the missed amount again when money next comes into your Kaskazi Everyday Account. Missed instalments are recorded on your loan and are reported to credit reference bureaus, which can make future borrowing harder.

If you think an instalment will be late, tell us before the due date. We cannot always waive the fee, but we can often agree a plan that avoids further missed payments. I can check your loan's next due date and amount if you'd like.

results.question: if the base rate goes up will my monthly payment on the loan change?
results.answer:

We write to you in the app before the change takes effect, telling you the new rate, your new instalment and the date it starts. Instalments already paid are not affected.

If the new instalment would be hard to manage, tell us. We will look at what we can do, such as a longer term within the limits in section 16.

results.question: My husband had a personal loan with you and he passed away last week. do we as the family have to keep paying it?
results.answer:
I'm very sorry for your loss. You do not have to keep paying the loan. Once the bank is told, we stop collecting instalments and stop charging late payment fees on the loan, and we make the credit life insurance claim; the family does not have to deal with the insurer. When the insurance pays, the loan is closed.

To notify us, a family member or the person handling the estate can tell us as soon as they can, at a branch or through the assistant, and give us a copy of the death certificate.

If any instalments were overdue before the date of death, we explain them to the person handling the estate and agree with them how they will be settled.

A colleague will reply in this chat, usually within about 5 minutes between 7:00 am and 10:00 pm, to help with the next steps.

results.question: which documents do i need for a personal loan? my salary goes to another bank
results.answer:

results.question: how is the personal loan interest worked out, is it linked to the base rate?

results.question: my student account what happens to it when i turn 26
results.answer:

If you finish your course before 26, your account becomes a Kaskazi Everyday Account, even if you are still 25 or younger. If you go back to study before you turn 26, you can ask for your account to be changed back to a Kaskazi Student Account by showing your new valid student ID.
